svg.text: BEST FOR: SRAM VS. HBM + SPECULATIVE DECODE 2.7X
FORMAT LINEAGE: Sahn Lam & Umar Jamil • EAGLE-2 / Medusa / FlashAttention-3
Why LLM Decoding Is Memory-Bound — and How Speculative Decoding Verifies 5 Tokens in 1 HBM Read
During decode, an H100 spends >95% of its time moving 70 GB of weights from HBM3e to SRAM for a single token. Draft-and-verify fixes the arithmetic intensity.
WHY DECODE IS MEMORY-BOUND: H100 GPU MEMORY PYRAMID
FlashAttention-3 tiles & Tensor Core registers live here
70B FP8 weights (70 GB) + Paged KV Cache live here
Cross-GPU Tensor Parallelism & Disaggregated KV DMA
Model: Llama-3.3-70B in FP8 (70 GB weights in HBM3e)
H100 SXM5 Peak FP8 Compute: 1,979 TFLOPS
Must stream all 70 GB weights from HBM -> SRAM
Min HBM transfer time = 70 GB / 3.35 TB/s = 20.9 ms
Arithmetic Intensity = ~2 FLOPs / Byte (! 98% Tensor Cores IDLE !)
FIX: Verify K=5 draft tokens in 1 weight read -> 5x arithmetic intensity!
SPECULATIVE DECODING TOKEN-TREE (DRAFT K=5 -> VERIFY IN 1 PASS)
STANDARD AUTOREGRESSIVE DECODE: 5 SEQUENTIAL 70B HBM READS = 160 ms
Bottleneck: Streaming 70 GB of weights 5 separate times = 350 GB moved from HBM to SRAM.
SPECULATIVE DRAFT-VERIFY LOOP (EAGLE-2 / MEDUSA): 1 SINGLE 70B HBM READ = 58 ms (2.7x FASTER)
2. TARGET 70B MODEL SCORES ALL 5 CANDIDATES IN 1 PARALLEL PASS
3. WHY IT IS MATHEMATICALLY LOSSLESS (EXACT TARGET DISTRIBUTION)
Target 70B computes logits for all K=5 draft positions in parallel. Using rejection sampling p_accept =
min(1, p_target(x) / p_draft(x)), any rejected token is resampled directly from the residual distribution —
guaranteeing 100% identical output quality to greedy or temperature sampling.
THREE SPECULATIVE DECODING ARCHITECTURES IN PRODUCTION

Rule: Prefill is compute-bound (optimize FLOPs with FlashAttention-3); Decode is HBM-bandwidth-bound (optimize tokens-per-weight-read with Speculative Decoding).
